subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Technical deep-dive latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (recap)

Alex / Priya, thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we covered, agreed pain points, and immediate next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inconsistent response tail latency during peak traffic for real-time recommendations (spikes to p95 ~1.2s for 512-token responses).
- Goal: achieve p95 < 200ms for 90% of queries, target p50 ~60
- Throughput expectation: 3k req/min steady, burst capacity to 6k req/min for promotional windows.

Model & inference requirements
- Primary model family: Acme plans to run a tuned LLM for product recommendations (~13B range) with preference for open licensing. They called out need for stateful KV cache support for multi-step contexts and session affinity for personalization.
- Quantization preference: acceptable to run int8-quantized model for cost reasons, but want quality check against float16 for top-10 recs.

Deployment topology discussed
- Proposed: Dedicated Redwood cluster in us-west-2 (customer-dedicated VPC) behind internal routing policy.
  - 3 replica groups across AZs for HA; autoscaling policy configured for target CPU/GPU utilization with headroom for 2x burst.
  - Cold-start mitigation: always-on warm pool of N instances (we estimated minimal warm pool of 4 80GB A10G-equivalent GPUs for baseline).
  - KV caching: enable prefix caching and session-affinity routing for repeat requests (will reduce per-token compute).
  - Fallback: quantized 8-bit variant for cost-sensitive tiers and a lower-cost smaller model for non-critical routes.

Open questions / risks
- Exact model choice (13B vs 7B) - affects GPU type and replication counts.
- Authentication / KMS integration for private deployment (they flagged internal KMS requirement).
- Procurement timelines - Acme prefers a single PO, needs draft MSA and price bands for Dedicated monthly commit.

Immediate next steps (agree on today)
1) Redwood to provide a capacity & cost estimate matrix (by model size + quantization + target p95) - deliverable: spreadsheet (we'll attach a first-pass). Owner: Marissa. ETA: Tue, 26 May.
2) Acme to confirm model preference and representative prompt set (10-20 canonical prompts) for quality validation. Owner: Alex / Priya. ETA: Mon, 25 May.
3) Schedule architecture workshop (1 hour) to lock down topology and autoscale settings - suggested times in email below. Owner: Connor to coordinate.
4) Redwood to send draft MSA + pricing bands for Dedicated commit. Owner: Marissa / Sales Ops. ETA: Wed, 27 May.

Attachments referenced: acme_latency_summary.xlsx (baseline telemetry), redwood_draft_msa.pdf (initial terms).

Thanks - I captured action owners inline. If that looks right, I will lock in the architecture workshop and start the capacity modeling.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 18:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (recap)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurately captures the discussion. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 3k req/min is our usual steady-state for recommendation API calls across our mobile and web clients. During marketing promos we see 2x spikes (hence 6k burst).
- Model preference: our ML team is leaning to a tuned Llama-2-13B derivative. We'll confirm the exact fork but plan on using an int8-quantized runtime for production.
- On KV caching: we definitely need session affinity for per-user context; curious if Redwood supports sharded session cache across replicas or if affinity must pin to a single replica.

We'll assemble the 15 prompts and shoot them over by Mon. Also, please send the cost matrix - we'll need it for procurement.

Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of ML Platform, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme-retail.com | +1 (212) 555-0932

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Technical deep-dive latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (recap)

Appreciate the quick clarifications Alex. Short answers to the two technical asks:
- Session affinity and sharded cache: Redwood supports both affinity and distributed cache layers. For strict session stickiness we can route sessions to a replica boundary plus a shared Redis-backed KV store for cross-replica reads (recommended for high availability). We'll include topology diagrams in the workshop.
- We'll include both float16 and int8 performance profiles in the capacity matrix so you can see quality vs cost tradeoffs.

Connor - can you run the first-pass capacity model assuming: Llama-2-13B int8 on 80GB A10G-equivalent GPUs, p95 target 200ms for 512 tokens, baseline steady 50 rps (3k/min), bursts to 100 rps. Include warm-pool sizing and expected token/sec throughput per GPU in the sheet. Tag any assumptions.

Dylan - please slot 60-minute workshop windows next week; prefer Tue/Wed afternoon PST. I'll propose times once you pull availability.

Alex / Priya - looking forward to the prompt set on Mon.

Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (recap)

Marissa - noted. I'll start the capacity model today. Quick note on assumptions I plan to document:
- Effective seq length for perf sizing: 512 tokens (avg 280 tokens per request observed in their sample).
- KV cache hit expected: 35% on first pass (we will sensitivity-run 20%/50%).
- Batching: aim for micro-batching at 5-10 ms scheduling windows to preserve tail latency.
- Warm pool: start with 4 GPUs, scale to 8 during burst (we'll provide costs).

I'll push the spreadsheet to the Drive link and flag questions for the workshop.

Connor
Lead Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
